hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's live attack as tenant A (alnoor) against tenant B (gulfsteel): API, query parameters, switch inputs, exports, files
hard_gates.evidence: I extended round 14's script to every list in the OpenAPI document (8 lists, adding numbering and currency) and to B's sequence, rate and currency ids (attack/attack.mjs). It made 158 operations, 1,006 documented query-parameter requests, 675 switch-input requests, 130 export/print requests and 35 filter/cursor requests. B had a canary user, private and shared saved views on all 8 lists, and a company logo file. Result: no B canary or B id in any answer. B's checksums for 22 tenant tables were unchanged, and A's list totals did not move when B wrote. The script flagged one item: DELETE /api/currency/rates/{B id} answered 204. Probing it showed this is not a leak. A's GET of that id is 404, B's row is unchanged afterwards, and A's DELETE of a random uuid also answers 204, so the delete is idempotent and says nothing about whether the id exists (attack/probe-delete.txt).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the database role the app uses
hard_gates.evidence: erp_app is not superuser, has no BYPASSRLS, cannot create roles and owns no table. Tables are owned by erp_owner. All 22 tables with tenant_id have it NOT NULL, with RLS enabled and forced and at least one policy (0 without). As erp_app with no tenant set, every table reads 0 rows. With tenant A set, it sees 0 of B's rows, and UPDATE of B's rows touches 0. Inserting a row with B's tenant_id is refused by the RLS policy. ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY gives 'must be owner', and row_security=off gives an error (db-roles-rls.txt, db-app-role-attack.txt).

hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions on the live product: a no-roles user is refused whatever the request looks like
hard_gates.evidence: noaccess@alnoor gets 403 on GET /api/identity/users with Host localhost:20050, app, app:8080, 127.0.0.1 and localhost, and with X-Forwarded-For 127.0.0.1 (no-roles-request-variants.txt). In the browser the no-roles user sees no menu and the API answers 403. The read-only user sees no New button and gets 403 on POST roles. After sign-out the API answers 401 (browser/walk.log).

hard_gates.evidence: I did not plant faults this round, so I have not tested whether the gates catch faults the real product does not have. The gates' own self-tests (GateSelfTests, the client-origin and own-id plant checks) passed in the verify, but they are the builder's plants, not mine. biggest_gap.title: The shared gates still cost too much per new endpoint, and this round's savings come from sending fewer attack values
biggest_gap.detail: In this round the HTTP attack sends fewer requests. Only the administrator's plain cookie session still sends every one of tenant B's route values. The tenant-switch headers and query, the bearer token, the refused callers and the Arabic sessions now send the first, middle and last value of each class (RouteValueClasses.PerClass = 3). Documented string parameters and list text filters now send 3 values per column instead of 8. This rests on the builder's claim that a handler behaves the same for every row of a table. That holds for the leaks the gates' self-tests plant, and nothing in the real product contradicts it. But I did not test it with my own plants this round. The cost problem the round was meant to fix is only partly fixed. My verify used 9,572 s of processor time against the 10,600 s maximum, about 1,000 s of headroom. The builder's own measurement says a GET endpoint without a route still costs about 14,000 attack requests (about 40 processor seconds), because of the undocumented-name matrix. So roughly 25 more such endpoints from p07, p12, p16 and later pieces would put every integration back over the limit, as happened in serial-12d. For a UAE trading or manufacturing company that means sales, purchasing, stock and VAT modules cannot be added without either raising the cap or thinning the gates further. The builder's record lists the remaining cuts as owner decisions.
biggest_gap.evidence: verify-critic-p00-foundation-r15.log: '[ratchet] verify processor time: 9572 s (dotnet 6857, web 2252, e2e 423, timing 40; maximum 10600 s)'. In the clone at e13b5003: tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G1/RouteValueClasses.cs (PerClass = 3), and G1HttpIsolationTests.cs, where the line 'if (!(variant == Variant.Plain && attacker == attackers[0]) && !representativePaths.Contains(path)) continue;' skips non-representative paths for every other variant. docs/decisions/p00-foundation-gate-cost.md, 'What was not cut' table: a GET endpoint without a route costs about 13,300 requests after the round. To reproduce: run ./erp verify at e13b5003 and read the ratchet processor-time line.

other_findings: I did not plant my own faults this round, so gate_gaps is empty because nothing was tested, not because no gaps exist. Gate backlog row 3 (G2 never varies the Host header; plant P13 from round 14) is still open: this round's gate code does not touch G2. On the real product, a no-roles user gets 403 with every Host value I tried, so this is not a product fault.

Since round 14 the product gained the numbering and currency modules (p10, p08). Their 8 lists, sequences, rates and currencies were in my live attack and leaked nothing. The G1 and G2 suites cover them, and both passed.

DELETE /api/currency/rates/{id} answers 204 for another tenant's id and for a random uuid without changing anything. This is not a leak, since the answer is the same as for an id that exists nowhere. It is noted so attack scripts do not misread it (attack/probe-delete.txt).
